qs.stem: What number comes next? 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, ?
steps: Look at the gaps between terms first; if they do not settle, try multiplying, squares, or two series taking turns.
Each term is double the previous plus 2.
Next term: 126.
Answer: 126.
qs.trap: Fixing on the first gap only. Check the rule on every term.

qs.stem: A sketchbook set marked at Rs 1200 is sold with a 25% discount, followed by a further 25% discount on the reduced price. What is the final price in rupees?
steps: After a further 25% off: 900 × 0.75 = 675.
The single equivalent discount is 43.75%, not 50%.
Answer: Rs 675.
qs.trap: Adding the discounts to get 50%. The second discount applies to the reduced price.

qs.stem: A mother is 4 times as old as her daughter. In 5 years she will be 3 times as old as her daughter. How old is the daughter now (in years)?
steps: Let the daughter be d years old, so the mother is 4d.
In 5 years: 4d + 5 = 3(d + 5).
Check: mother 40, in 5 years 45 = 3 × 15. Answer: 10.
qs.trap: Adding the years to only one person. Both get older by the same amount.

qs.stem: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the two numbers add up to 9? (Give your answer correct to two decimal places.)
steps: There are 6 × 6 = 36 equally likely outcomes.
Pairs that add to 9: (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3), so 4 ways.
Probability = 4/36 = 0.1111.
Correct to two decimals: 0.11 (answers from 0.11 to 0.12 accepted).
qs.trap: Counting (2,6) and (6,2) as one outcome. Order matters with two different dice.

qs.stem: A train 120 m long runs at 72 km/h. How many seconds does it take to cross a platform 400 m long completely?
steps: To clear the platform the train must cover its own length plus the platform: 120 + 400 = 520 m.
Speed in m/s: 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s.
Answer: 26 seconds.
qs.trap: Using only the platform length, or forgetting to convert km/h to m/s.

qs.stem: How many diagonals does a convex polygon with 7 sides have?
steps: From each corner you can draw a diagonal to every other corner except itself and its two neighbours: 7 − 3 = 4.
7 corners × 4 = 28, but each diagonal is counted from both ends.
Diagonals = 28 ÷ 2 = 14.
Answer: 14.

qs.stem: Gear 1 turns clockwise. Which of these gears turn clockwise?
steps: Gear 1 turns clockwise (red arrow).
Rules: meshing gears turn opposite ways; an open belt keeps the same direction; a crossed belt reverses the direction.
Links: 1→2: belt (same), 2→3: mesh (reverses), 3→4: mesh (reverses), 4→5: mesh (reverses), 5→6: belt (same).
Directions: 1 C, 2 C, 3 A, 4 C, 5 A, 6 A (C = clockwise). So the clockwise gears are gear 2, gear 4.
qs.trap: Treating every belt like a mesh. An open belt does not reverse the direction.

qs.stem: Which of these are usually called warm colours?
steps: Warm colours remind us of fire and sunlight: reds, oranges and yellows.
Cool colours remind us of water and sky: blues, greens and violets.
Warm colours seem to come forward; cool colours seem to recede.
So red, orange and yellow are warm.
Correct: Red; Orange; Yellow. Not correct: Blue.
qs.trap: Counting every bright colour as warm.

qs.stem: Which of these are chemical changes?
steps: A chemical change makes a new substance.
Rust, curd and ash with smoke are new substances.
Melting ice is still water, so it is a physical change.
Physical changes are usually easy to reverse.
Correct: Milk turning into curd; Paper burning; An iron gate rusting. Not correct: Ice melting.
qs.trap: Counting melting as chemical. The substance stays the same.

qs.stem: Warli paintings use simple circles, triangles and lines in white on a mud background. Which community made this style famous?
opts: The Gond tribe of Madhya Pradesh
The Toda people of the Nilgiris
steps: Warli art is made by the Warli tribe in the Sahyadri region of Maharashtra.
Figures are built from circles, triangles and lines.
White rice paste on a mud wall is traditional.
Answer: the Warli tribe of Maharashtra. That is option D.
qs.trap: Confusing Warli with Gond art, which uses dots and dashes in bright colours.

qs.stem: A screwdriver with a thicker handle is easier to turn. Why?
opts: A wider handle gives a larger turning effect for the same grip force
A thick handle reduces friction on the screw
steps: A screwdriver is a wheel and axle: the handle is the wheel, the shaft is the axle.
Turning effect = force × radius.
A larger handle radius gives more turning effect at the shaft.
So less effort is needed. (Option A.)
qs.trap: Thinking the weight matters. The radius of the handle matters.

qs.stem: Charles Correa, Laurie Baker and B. V. Doshi were all:
steps: All three were architects who shaped modern Indian buildings.
B. V. Doshi won the Pritzker Prize, architecture's top award, in 2018.
Laurie Baker was known for low-cost brick buildings in Kerala.
Answer: architects. That is option B.
qs.trap: Not recognising the names. Designers should know India's great architects.

qs.stem: What is ergonomics mainly concerned with?
opts: Designing products to suit the human body and how people use them
steps: Ergonomics studies human size, strength, reach and comfort.
Chair heights, handle grips and keyboard layouts are examples.
The aim is safety, comfort and efficiency.
Cost and branding are separate concerns. (Option D.)
qs.trap: Thinking it is about looks. It is about fit and comfort.

qs.stem: At the same moment, a 3 m pole casts a shadow 4 m long and a tower casts a shadow 16 m long. How tall is the tower?
steps: The sun's rays are parallel, so height ÷ shadow is the same for both objects.
Pole: 3 ÷ 4.
Answer: 12 m.
qs.trap: Adding the difference in shadow lengths. Use the ratio, not the difference.

qs.stem: Jaipur's blue pottery is unusual among Indian pottery because:
opts: It is fired without any heat
It is made from quartz-based paste rather than ordinary clay
It is made from river sand only
steps: Jaipur blue pottery uses a dough of quartz powder, glass and other materials.
It is decorated mostly in blue and white and glazed.
Its roots trace to Persian and Mughal influence.
Answer: it is quartz-based, not clay. That is option B.
qs.trap: Assuming all pottery is made from clay.

qs.stem: Madhubani painting, known for bold outlines and paintings that fill every space with detail, comes from which state?
steps: Madhubani (or Mithila) painting comes from the Mithila region of Bihar.
It was traditionally painted on walls and floors by women.
Bold outlines and densely filled patterns are typical.
Answer: Bihar. That is option D.
qs.trap: Confusing it with Pattachitra from Odisha.

qs.stem: In a code language, DESIGN is written as BCQGEL. How is POSTER written in the same code?
steps: Compare letter by letter: D → B, E → C.
Each letter moves 2 places back in the alphabet (Z wraps to A).
Apply it to POSTER: P→N, O→M, S→Q, T→R, E→C, R→P.
Answer: NMQRCP.
qs.trap: Shifting in the wrong direction. Check the rule on two letters before applying it.

qs.stem: Why is a fuse included in a household electric circuit?
opts: It makes appliances use less power
It melts and breaks the circuit when the current becomes too high
steps: A fuse is a thin wire with a low melting point.
Too much current heats the wire.
It melts and breaks the circuit before wires overheat.
Circuit breakers do the same job and can be reset. (Option C.)
qs.trap: Thinking a fuse stores power. It is a safety device.

qs.stem: In a certain leap year, 1 January is a Tuesday. What day of the week is 10 May in that year?
steps: Days from 1 January to 10 May: 31 + 29 + 31 + 30 + 9 = 130.
130 = 7 × 18 + 4, so the weekday moves on by 4.
Tuesday + 4 days = Saturday.
Answer: Saturday.
qs.trap: Counting 1 January itself as a day to move on. Start from day 0. Also remember February has 29 days in a leap year.

qs.stem: Gear P has 60 teeth and turns clockwise at 90 revolutions per minute. It meshes with gear Q, which has 20 teeth. How fast and in which direction does Q turn?
steps: Teeth pass the meeting point at the same rate on both gears.
Teeth per minute from P = 60 × 90 = 5400.
Q turns 5400 ÷ 20 = 270 times a minute.
Meshing gears turn opposite ways, so Q turns anticlockwise at 270 rpm.
qs.trap: Thinking the bigger gear turns faster. The smaller gear turns faster.

qs.trap: Reading one clue backwards. "A is faster than B" puts A above B.

qs.stem: Why does ice float on water?
opts: Ice is denser than liquid water
Air bubbles in ice always make it float
Ice is less dense than liquid water
steps: When water freezes, its molecules lock into an open pattern.
This takes up more space, so ice is about 9% less dense than water.
Anything less dense than water floats.
This is why lakes freeze from the top down. (Option D.)
qs.trap: Thinking ice is heavier because it is solid. Water is unusual in this way.

qs.stem: A logo must look sharp on a business card and on a huge banner. Which kind of file is best?
opts: A bitmap made of large pixels
A vector file, built from mathematical paths
steps: Raster images (JPEG, PNG) are made of pixels and blur or go blocky when enlarged.
Vector files (such as SVG) store shapes as paths.
They can be scaled to any size without losing sharpness.
That is why logos are made as vectors. (Option C.)
qs.trap: Choosing a high-quality JPEG. Any pixel image breaks down when enlarged enough.
